claims.text: The as-synthesized nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs solid solution has a homogeneous, random atomic distribution.
Hydrogen treatment at 300°C for 2 hours will induce surface atomic rearrangement in PtPdRhRuIrOs.
The specified treatment can induce surface rearrangement without bulk sintering.
Reducing-atmosphere thermal treatment will cause selective surface segregation of one or more constituent elements.
Pt may become enriched at the catalyst surface following treatment.
Surface segregation will alter the local active-site ensemble structure.
Surface segregation will shift the catalyst's d-band center.
The altered surface composition will change the binding energies of ethanol-oxidation species.
Changes in intermediate binding will shift ethanol-oxidation pathway energetics.
Preferential stabilization of the proposed pathway will promote more complete ethanol oxidation.
Pt-rich surface domains may facilitate C-C bond cleavage and subsequent oxidation steps.
The untreated random surface favors a mixed distribution of ethanol-oxidation products.
The treated catalyst will have greater selectivity toward complete oxidation products, including a higher CO2 yield, than the untreated baseline.
Overall catalytic activity after treatment will differ from the untreated baseline by no more than about 10%.
The proposed effect should hold for treatment temperatures of approximately 250–350°C.
The proposed effect should hold during ethanol oxidation at 50–70°C in acidic electrolyte.
Treatments above 400°C may cause sintering and fail to produce the proposed segregation behavior.
Non-reductive treatment atmospheres may fail to produce the proposed surface segregation.
XPS or LEIS can measure the treatment-induced change in surface elemental composition.
A surface-composition difference and a CO2-selectivity shift can be tested against approximately 5% decision thresholds using treated and untreated controls.
